title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
description:
Evaluate an arithmetic expression written in Reverse Polish Notation (postfix): operands come first and each operator applies to the two values just before it. The operators are +, -, * and /. Division of integers truncates toward zero (so 7 / -2 is -3, not -4).

Input format
One line: the tokens separated by single spaces. Each token is an integer or one of + - * /.

Output format
The integer value of the expression.
constraints: 1 <= number of tokens <= 10000. The expression is valid and never divides by zero. All intermediate values fit in a 64-bit signed integer.
hints: When you read a number you cannot use it yet. Where could you keep numbers until an operator needs them?
Use a stack: push numbers; on an operator pop two values b then a (b is the top), compute a op b, and push the result.

For division, truncate toward zero. In Python use int(a / b) for small values or compute with absolute values and restore the sign; // rounds toward negative infinity and is wrong for negative results.
